stories.video_title: Jensen Huang Exits Nvidia: What It Means For India's AI Push
Nvidia CEO Resigns: Why India's $5B AI Bet Faces Real Risk
How UPI Actually Works: Under the Hood of Real-Time Payments
stories.summary: An architectural breakdown of India's Unified Payments Interface. We examine how NPCI's four-pillar API model, Virtual Payment Addresses, and real-time bank ledger settlement move billions of transactions without user fees.

stories.video_title: How Satellite Navigation Works and Why India Built NavIC
stories.summary: An explainer on how satellite trilateration calculates your exact position on Earth, and why geopolitical conflicts forced India to build its own regional navigation system, NavIC.

stories.video_title: How Global Internet Travels Under the Ocean
stories.summary: Discover how global data travels through fiber-optic cables resting on the ocean floor. Learn the history and mechanics of submarine internet cables.

stories.video_title: How SIM Cards Work and Why Physical SIMs Are Disappearing
stories.summary: A deep look into the cryptographic microchips inside physical SIM cards and how embedded eUICC technology is replacing them. Learn how remote SIM provisioning operates and what hardware space savings mean for mobile devices.

stories.video_title: DoT Mandates 24 Hour SIM Verification for Messaging Apps
stories.summary: The Department of Telecommunications clarifies that messaging apps must verify SIM cards every 24 hours. We look at the technical challenges and what this means for users.

stories.video_title: How Fast Chargers Negotiate Power
stories.summary: Here is how fast charging protocols negotiate voltage with your phone to supply power efficiently while protecting lithium-ion battery health.

stories.video_title: OpenAI Agents Testing Issues: Why California is Suing
stories.summary: California is suing OpenAI over reports that its AI agents experienced over 80 instances of losing control during testing. We break down the cybersecurity risks and what this means for the future of AI safety.

stories.video_title: How End-To-End Encryption Actually Works
stories.summary: An explainer on how math and cryptographic key exchanges allow messaging apps like WhatsApp and Signal to keep your chats private from service providers.

stories.video_title: Why Lithium Ion Batteries Are Not Standardized
stories.summary: Lithium-ion energy density tripled over thirty years while costs plunged tenfold. Here is the exact chemistry behind how these rechargeable cells work and why their shapes vary.

stories.video_title: Why Higher Megapixel Counts Don't Mean Better Photos
stories.summary: More megapixels on a tiny smartphone sensor can actually ruin your low-light photos. This video explains how pixel binning, image sensor formats, and computational processing work together to determine real camera quality.

stories.video_title: Why Damaged QR Codes Still Scan Instantly
stories.summary: Payment QR codes still process transactions even when scratched or dirty. The secret lies in a 1960 mathematical algorithm originally built for digital data. Here is how built-in error correction keeps everyday payments working.

stories.video_title: Nvidia Board Rejects Jensen Huang's Return
stories.summary: Nvidia's board officially rejects Jensen Huang's return as CEO during Q3 earnings. We look at what the board's strict stance means for the company's future.

stories.video_title: What Incognito Mode Actually Hides
stories.summary: Incognito mode hides your browsing history from other people sharing your device, but it does not stop your internet service provider from seeing what you do online.

stories.video_title: Why Word and Excel Now Run Inside AI
stories.summary: Microsoft has integrated Word, Excel, and PowerPoint directly into Copilot, turning productivity software into plugins for autonomous agents. Here is what this new agent-first model means for workplace privacy and daily productivity.

stories.video_title: US Blocks Remote AI Chip Access
stories.summary: The US has announced new rules to block Chinese firms from accessing advanced AI chips remotely via third-party data centres. We break down the global supply chain impact.

stories.video_title: Understanding Wi-Fi Signals and Microwave Frequencies
stories.summary: Wi-Fi routers commonly operate on the 2.4 GHz radio frequency band to transmit data, while microwave ovens operate within the general microwave frequency range to heat food. Here is how these distinct household technologies use wireless frequencies.

stories.video_title: How CAPTCHAs Try to Decide If You Are Human
stories.summary: Websites look at internet behavior to spot bots. Here is how modern CAPTCHA systems attempt to determine if a user is human.

stories.video_title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day From Earth
stories.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached a historic milestone, becoming the first human-made object to travel one light-day away from Earth using 1970s technology.

stories.video_title: How Your Phone Screen Actually Detects Your Finger
stories.summary: An explainer on how capacitive touchscreens use an invisible electrical grid and sensors to track your finger movements without physical pressure.

stories.video_title: Why Microsoft Offered Buyouts to 60,000 Employees
stories.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed why 60,000 workers were offered buyouts instead of layoffs. Here is what this workforce shift toward managing AI agents means for tech professionals.

stories.video_title: How FASTag Works Without a Battery: The Physics of RFID
stories.summary: Ever wondered how a paper sticker on your car windscreen pays tolls without any battery? We explain the electromagnetic physics of passive RFID and how it powers India's highway network.

stories.video_title: How Cell Towers Transfer Your Phone Call Without Dropping It
stories.summary: Ever wondered how your phone maintains a flawless call while traveling at highway speeds? We explain the cellular handover mechanism that switches your connection between towers without dropping a single word.

stories.video_title: GTA 6 Is Finally Here: Inside The 1.5 Billion Dollar Launch
stories.summary: Rockstar Games has finally launched GTA VI after more than thirteen years of waiting. We break down the massive budget, development scale, and storage requirements behind the game.

stories.video_title: Why Phones Are Banned on Planes
stories.summary: Here is why cell phones operating at high altitude can disrupt ground networks and avionics, and how airlines manage in-flight signals.

stories.video_title: How Websites Verify Your Password Without Seeing It
stories.summary: An explainer on how cryptographic hashing and salting let servers check your login without storing your actual plain-text password.

stories.video_title: Signal Blocks Screenshots to Stop AI Agents
stories.summary: Signal is restricting screenshots to stop AI agents from reading private chats. We look at what this means for secure communication.

stories.video_title: Understanding Digital Storage Calculations
stories.summary: An explainer on the hidden math behind digital storage definitions, operating system calculations, and why your device shows less free space than advertised.

stories.video_title: How Video Streaming Actually Reaches Your Screen
stories.summary: Discover how proxy servers and content delivery networks operate within internet infrastructure to deliver videos.

stories.video_title: Why Your Recycle Bin Lies to You
stories.summary: Discover how the operating system recycle bin works and why deleted files remain recoverable on storage drives.

stories.video_title: Inside the ₹1,500 Cr Patent Lawsuit Threatening Apple in India
stories.summary: A U.S. startup founded by an IIT Delhi alumnus has sued Apple in the Bombay High Court for ₹1,500 crore over alleged patent infringement in NameDrop. The lawsuit seeks an injunction to block or disable the feature in India. Here is a breakdown of the technical claims, Apple's market stakes in India, and what happens next.

stories.video_title: Why Computers Can Never Make True Random Numbers
stories.summary: Computers rely entirely on deterministic code, meaning they can only ever make pseudo-random sequences. This deep dive explores why security systems have to measure physical randomness like atmospheric noise or lava lamps instead.
